messages:
Avery (Support): Hey team, Zoe from PayFlow reports their production integration started getting 429s around 09:04 UTC. They say it looks like sudden request bursts causing RPM/TPM limits to trip. Can someone triage?

Zoe (Customer): yep, we saw ~1.2k requests in a 30s window from our main backend. Most requests are identical template-completions. We already added exponential backoff but it's still frequent.

Mateo (SRE): Catching up — can you paste a sample request header and the X-Request-IDs? Also which API key/project?

Zoe (Customer): Project: pf-prod-42, API key ends with ...8Gz. Sample header: `Authorization: Bearer sk-pf-xxxx`, `X-Request-ID: pf-20260315-0722-9a7d`.

Avery (Support): Replayed a small slice of the last minute logs for pf-prod-42. Quick summary: 09:04:12-09:04:40 shows ~1,150 requests; 95% from 3 IPs belonging to their egress cluster. Rate limit response headers from our gateway looked like: `x-rate-limit-rpm: 600`, `x-rate-limit-tpm: 100000`, `retry-after: 15`.

Priya (ProdEng): Two quick things to check: 1) Are those requests small token-wise? TPM is token-based (per-minute tokens) while RPM is request-count. If they batch many short requests they hit RPM first. 2) Do they have streaming vs non-streaming toggles? Streaming can reduce token counts per request.

Lin (CSE): Zoe, can you confirm client library version and whether the requests are synchronous retries or new user actions? Means: are these retries piling up creating a retry storm?

Zoe (Customer): Using payflow-sdk v1.4.2. Our app fan-outs a request to three downstreams and each does a call to Redwood. It is not a retry loop — the frontend triggers multiple concurrent requests for the same user action.

Mateo (SRE): That explains spike shape. Short concurrent identical requests => RPM explosion. Immediate mitigation options: 1) add a local coalescing layer in their app (debounce/queue duplicate calls), 2) request a temporary RPM increase on their project while they deploy fix, 3) enable per-route caching on our side for that endpoint if responses are identical.

Avery (Support): Zoe — would you like us to open a temporary RPM bump? We'll need approval and an ETA for your client-side fix.

Zoe (Customer): Yes please, a temporary bump for 1 hour while we roll a debounce patch. ETA: 25 minutes.

Priya (ProdEng): I'll prepare a safe bump: +1000 RPM for pf-prod-42 for 1 hour, no TPM change. That should keep token budget intact and stop 429s. Mateo - any concerns re capacity?

Mateo (SRE): +1000 RPM is fine given cluster headroom; watch per-node CPU. I'll add a short alert rule to watch 5m p95 latency and 429 rate for that key.

ratebot: Action logged: temporary rpm_increase request for pf-prod-42 by Priya at 1769100145, expires in 3600s.

Mateo (SRE): Also captured a snippet from the gateway logs showing the throttle decisions: ```
[09:04:18] key=pf-prod-42 reqs_in_min=1124 rpm_limit=600 decision=throttle reason="rpm_exceeded" top_ips=[10.11.23.4,10.11.23.5,10.11.23.6]
[09:04:18] response_headers: x-rate-limit-rpm=600 x-rate-limit-tpm=100000 retry-after=15
```

Avery (Support): For postmortem/education, runbook notes we should share with customer: - implement jittered exponential backoff with capped max attempts - add client-side dedupe/coalescing for identical requests - use streaming where appropriate to lower token usage - include X-Request-ID in retries for easier correlation

Lin (CSE): Zoe — I'll send a GitHub gist with a small debounce middleware for payflow-sdk that intercepts identical payloads for 1s and coalesces responses. That should be a minimal change.

Zoe (Customer): Thanks — applying patch now. After applying we did a quick test on staging and concurrent calls collapsed from 250->2 within 500ms.

Priya (ProdEng): After the bump went in at 1769100145, SRE telemetry shows 429s dropped to ~0.1% within 30s. Keep us posted if anything else surfaces.

Avery (Support): Closing loop: Zoe, will you confirm when you finished the deploy and we can rollback the temporary RPM bump?

Zoe (Customer): Deployed at 09:28 UTC, verified in prod traffic logs. No further 429s. Please remove the bump when convenient.

Priya (ProdEng): Bump scheduled to auto-expire; I've cancelled early at 1769100360. Removed.

Mateo (SRE): Final recommendations for internal KB: - prefer RPM-first mitigation for fanout bursts - route customers to per-route caching or coalescing patterns - provide a small client-side debounce example in docs - consider a new Console hint for projects with high short-burst RPM/low TPM profile

Avery (Support): Thanks everyone. I'll follow up with Zoe via email with runbook + our debounce gist and close the ticket. :thumbsup:
